analysis:
Integration of the three units. The PR adds a `purpose` (provider | desktop_account) to the console device-link approval flow. It is read from the `?purpose=` query string (link/page.tsx), sent in the POST body by DeviceLinkForm.tsx, and forwarded unchanged by the Next proxy route. It also adds the console-ui.md documentation update, a changelog entry and tests. Nothing touches the provider process, the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket, attestation, keys, App Attest authorization or prefix-cache storage, so T-041, TB-007, TB-011 and T-053 are unaffected.

I discarded two candidate findings from unit 1. (1) The post-approval UI check at DeviceLinkForm.tsx:62 is UX only. It is a worry only if the coordinator ignores `purpose`, but the changelog states the coordinator enforces purpose mismatch server-side, and no source here shows otherwise. The concern also rests on an assumed deployment state, and it is an instance of the existing device-code phishing class. (2) The missing threat-model entry for a 30-day read-only desktop token is not a gap in this retained model. Console UI and backend token issuance are explicitly out of scope; the platform-owned model covers them, and A-008 here describes provider custody of provider tokens.

Coverage limits: the coordinator's device-approve handler and the desktop token scope enforcement were not supplied. The console routes were not checked against the doc claims in console-ui.md, which record existing behavior only (GA consent defaulting to granted, Datadog RUM replay, unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval in script-src, ignoreBuildErrors). I found no concrete security regression in this PR.
